name: rounding-order/slow-is-decimal-exact-90x3
source: game: Hook.ModifyDamage (one decimal through the additive and multiplicative modifiers, the caps after, one int cast)
doc: 90 x 1.3 = 117 exactly in decimal. Slow's multiplier counts the cards played this turn (SlowAmount), so the scenario plays them; an applied amount does not set it.

xfail_engines.old: old multiplies the int damage by 1f + 0.1f * count in float32, so 90 x 1.3 truncates to 116 where the game's one decimal chain gives 117 (fix/rounding-order 2935e9ff not landed).
xfail_engines.core2: old multiplies the int damage by 1f + 0.1f * count in float32, so 90 x 1.3 truncates to 116 where the game's one decimal chain gives 117 (fix/rounding-order 2935e9ff not landed). core2 runs old's rules until its family switch is on (migrated_families.json), so it fails the same way.
